messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired (PD-98214) — INFERENCE QUEUE backlog > 95th percentile for 2m (us-west-prod). Autocascade not recovering. Impact: increased latency and 5xxs for some customers.

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty page created: PD-98214 — Auto-escalation to eng-oncall.

aj: acked — I’m oncall. Pinging infra and runtime. Any recent deploys?

maya: no deploys in last 30m from prod-main. Seeing autoscaler metrics spike: node provisioning stalled, kube API requeues high.

sam: looking at queue length now — backlog ~18k reqs across dispatcher. 99th p90 token latency up ~3x. Some prefix warmups failing.

leo: can we snapshot the hot job pods and check KV cache warmup counters? I’ll tail dispatcher logs.

sam: tailing dispatcher logs:
```
2026-03-15T09:12:03Z dispatcher-7f6d: enqueue time 0.9s -> backlog 18321
2026-03-15T09:12:10Z autoscaler-controller: provision request queued, quota=0, retrying
2026-03-15T09:12:32Z kvcache-warmup: miss-rate 0.86, slow-warmup 124s
```

mayа: (note: maya re-posting) miss-rate is huge — KV cache warmup failing due to too many unique prefixes from a few high-throughput customers. This is causing long tail token generation and inflating batch sizes.

aj: customer impact? any 5xx visible?

sam: yes — approx 12% of requests to hosted/v1/generate are returning 504 or timing out in us-west over last 4m. Affected routes: /v1/generate-heavy, /v1/chat-stream. Not global yet but escalating.

leo: immediate mitigation plan: 1) manual scale dedicated pool (spin x4 on-demand nodes) 2) enable fallback routing to smaller-latency model for non-enterprise tenants 3) rate-limit noisy prefixes for 10m. I can run manual scale if ops approves.

ops-bot: manual pool spinup requires infra approval due to spot pools. Requesting run: `infra/approve scale-request-4765432100`

aj: approve. Execute manual scale and apply temporary rate-limit on the top 5 prefixes by qps. Post commands here.

leo: running scale command now:
```
# spin up 4 on-demand gpus in us-west
infractl pools add --region us-west --size 4 --type on-demand --tag "pd-98214-temp"
kubectl patch deployment autoscaler -n inference -p '{"spec":{"replicas":6}}'
```

sam: started. autoscaler events: provisioning -> pending -> running for 3 nodes. One node stuck with image pull backoff (nodepool capacity inconsistency).

maya: applying rate-limit rule (temp):
```
consolecli routes update --route /v1/generate-heavy --ratelimit 200/min --scope prefix:top5
```

aj: enabling fallback routing to small-latency model (redwood-small-v2) for non-P0 tenants:
```
routingctl set-fallback --from-model redwood-llama-3 --to-model redwood-small-v2 --scope non-p0 --duration 20m
```

sam: after manual scale + rate-limit + fallback: backlog dropped from 18k -> 6.2k in ~90s. 504s reduced to ~3.4%. Latency p95 improving slowly.

leo: note: one on-demand node failed earlier; infra team spinning replacement. I’ll keep an eye on warmup counters.

ops-bot: infractl reports new nodes healthy: 3/4 provisioned OK, 1 replaced. Nodepool rebalance in progress.

pagerduty-bot: PD-98214 acknowledged by aj, in progress.

aj: good work. Quick customer impact summary for folks triaging: 
- window: 09:11–09:17 UTC (mitigation started ~09:12)
- peak backlog: ~18.3k
- peak error rate: ~12% 504s in us-west for generation endpoints
- affected customers: subset of hosted customers with high prefix-variance (tbd list)
- mitigation: manual on-demand spin, rate-limited top noisy prefixes, fallback routing to smaller model

maya: posting runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/autoscaler-warmup-lag (see steps 2a–2d for KV cache).

sam: recommend follow-up actions: - increase kvcache parallel warmup workers by 2 - add guardrail to detect prefix-cardinality spikes and auto-throttle by prefix - run postmortem to adjust autoscaler headroom.

aj: agree. assigning postmortem to sam + maya + leo. Please collect timeline and metric graphs (dispatcher QPS, kvcache miss rate, node provisioning events).

leo: leaving the channel, handing off to maya for next 30m watch. maya — you have the rotation.

maya: taking over. I’ll monitor for 20m then hand to infra-ops for long tail.

ops-bot: note added to PD: temporary scaling tag pd-98214-temp; removing after 60m unless otherwise requested.

pagerduty-bot: PD-98214 status: acknowledged -> escalated -> in progress.

aj: closing update — system trending stable, backlog < 2k, error rate back to ~1.2%. We’ll keep the temp nodes for 60m and then scale down. Filing postmortem. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: PD-98214 — paging resolved (ACK maintained). Please file postmortem within 48h.

maya: noted — will create a postmortem draft and link ops graphs.

sam: adding quick commands used for runbook notes:
```
infractl pools add --region us-west --size 4 --type on-demand --tag "pd-98214-temp"
kubectl patch deployment autoscaler -n inference -p '{"spec":{"replicas":6}}'
consolecli routes update --route /v1/generate-heavy --ratelimit 200/min --scope prefix:top5
routingctl set-fallback --from-model redwood-llama-3 --to-model redwood-small-v2 --scope non-p0 --duration 20m
```

leo: final: recommend adding a modest standby headroom for KV-heavy workloads (2x warmup workers) and a tuned prefix-cardinality alert before paging.

aj: thanks all. handing to postmortem owners.

(Reaction summary: :eyes: @sam, :rocket: @leo, :white_check_mark: @aj)
